transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Linda Park (Pinegrove Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Pinegrove CTO), Sofia Gomez (Pinegrove Platform)

Summary:
Quarterly business review and health check focused on usage trends, unit costs, reliability incidents over the past quarter, and roadmap alignment for Pinegrove's plan to expand production usage to customer support and internal search. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted for predictable throughput, routing by region for data residency, and KMS/SAML questions for compliance. Agreed to run an in-house benchmark and follow up with pricing proposal for reserved capacity.

Topics:
- Usage and cost trends (tokens, embeddings)
- Reliability incidents and SLA gaps
- Roadmap: Dedicated capacity and model recommendations
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
- Next steps: benchmarks and pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we wanted to make this QBR pretty pragmatic, run through the usage numbers, costs, any reliability stuff, and then next steps. Linda, Marcus, are we good to go?
[00:12] Linda: Yep, totally. Thanks Alex. We've got, uh, about 15 minutes of agenda items from our side, but mostly curious about the dedicated numbers and the forecast you sent last week — the one with the breakouts for chat versus embeddings.
[00:25] Marcus: And to add, we have exec budget reviews coming up early July so timeline's tight for any reserved capacity proposals.
[00:33] Priya: Understood — we'll try to keep it tight. Ravi, do you want to start on the reliability and perf summary?
[00:39] Ravi: Sure. So quick snapshot — over the last 90 days Pinegrove has averaged ~320M tokens/month on hosted, embeddings are about 45k vectors/month, bursty during product launches. We've seen tail latency spikes on long chat sessions, which correlate with sequence lengths over 1.5k tokens. There were two alert windows in May where latency exceeded the 95th percentile target — both were due to noisy async batch backlog on the multi-tenant pool.
[01:10] Sofia: That matches our monitoring; we saw a couple of timeout retries in our sidecar that matched the same windows. Not catastrophic, but it did trigger a rollback on a small release.
[01:20] Alex: Right, and those were the ones where the automatic fallback routed to the smaller model variant which increased token cost per output, yes?
[01:26] Ravi: Correct, the fallback kept requests alive but used a different model instance which changed cost and slightly changed output quality.
[01:33] Linda: On quality, we've noticed some hallucination regressions with the smaller variant on multi-step instructions, so that's a concern for support workflows.
[01:40] Ravi: Totally, that's a tradeoff. Our recommendation for that pattern is Dedicated with pinned model variants and proactive KV cache warming — reduces both latency and regression risk.
[01:52] Marcus: Can you quantify the cost delta for dedicated? The CFO asked for a per-1M-token estimate including infra amortization.
[01:59] Alex: We can model that. Last week I sent a draft spreadsheet; we'll update that with the dedicated reserved numbers. For rough ballpark, dedicated usually moves unit cost down by 25–40% depending on batch sizes and cache hit rates.
[02:12] Linda: That's promising. Our current concern is predictable throughput — we need <150ms median and 95th under 600ms for short queries (<=256 tokens). Does Dedicated hit that?
[02:22] Ravi: Yes, with the right GPU config and continuous batching controls we can hit that. Median 100–120ms, 95th under 400ms in our internal tests for that profile. We'll run an explicit benchmark on your prompt set to confirm.
[02:36] Sofia: On the security side, we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration and whether keys remain in our cloud account for private. Also SSO/SAML SCIM provisioning — we've got strict provisioning requirements.
[02:48] Priya: Pinegrove, we already shared the SOC 2 summary in the portal but I'll push the full report and the SSO guide. For Private deployments keys can stay in customer-managed KMS, yes. For Dedicated there's a managed option but we can do customer-managed keys with an enterprise contract.
[03:05] Marcus: Great. A follow-up: any data residency routing options? Some EU customers require EU-only processing.
[03:12] Alex: Yes, routing by policy is available; requests can be pinned to region or fallback to nearest compatible region. We'll note that in your proposal.
[03:20] Linda: Back to reliability — you mentioned cache warming. Is that something your runtime automates or do we need to prepopulate?
[03:28] Ravi: There's both. The runtime does prefix/KV caching automatically for repeated contexts, but for first-party cold starts we recommend a short warm-up job to prime the cache for known prompt families. We can provide a cache-warm script and runbook.
[03:41] Linda: Good. About the hallucination issue — any recommended evals or guardrails we should be using? We run unit tests against prompts but need more systematic regression detection.
[03:50] Priya: Redwood Optimize can surface quality regressions tied to prompt sets — you can upload a set and get alerts on metric drift. We also recommended function-calling or structured outputs for high-risk flows to reduce hallucinations.
[04:03] Sofia: Function-calling looks useful, but will it affect latency?
[04:08] Ravi: It adds a small orchestration overhead, but overall it often reduces downstream cost because you avoid parsing errors and retries; net latency is comparable for simple calls.
[04:18] Marcus: Ok, timeline wise — we need a commercial proposal by July 6 to present to finance July 9. Is that doable?
[04:25] Alex: Yes — I'll send reserved capacity options and term lengths by Friday, 7/2. I'll include the per-1M-token cost, expected monthly spend, and the assumptions for batch sizes and cache-hit rates.
[04:34] Linda: And can you include an option for a small pilot (4-week dedicated trial) so we can validate perf without long commitment?
[04:41] Alex: We can do a pilot for a short term — typically that's an add-on to the reserved contract, or sometimes we run a time-limited dedicated pool with usage caps. I'll include both options.
[04:51] Sofia: Related, what's the SLA for Dedicated? We saw ~99.9% historically but need clarity on credits and objectives.
[04:58] Priya: Dedicated comes with an SLA tier — 99.95% with enterprise plan and advanced support. We'll add the exact credit calculations in the proposal.
[05:08] Marcus: On the tech deep dive, Ravi, can you run through the benchmark plan?
[05:12] Ravi: Plan is: 1) get sample prompt set (Sofia to share), 2) run a 1M-token benchmark across your main model variants (we'll test base and quantized where relevant), 3) capture median/95/99 latencies, cost per 1k tokens, and output diffs for a subset. We'll share a spreadsheet and raw logs. Expected run time 24–48 hours once we have the prompt set and keys.
[05:35] Sofia: I'll upload the sample prompt set to the shared folder today — mostly multi-turn support dialogs and some retrieval-augmented prompts.
[05:42] Ravi: Great. Also, we need an S3 bucket or secure upload for the corpus; we can pull it if you give read access, or we can run it in your VPC for Private/Dedicated if you prefer.
[05:55] Linda: We'll share a presigned URL.
[05:58] Alex: Quick question from finance angle — do you have any concerns around spend predictability? Are you currently seeing cost surprises?
[06:05] Linda: Our engineers optimized prompts but there were occasional spikes during launches; the current hosted plan made it hard to forecast because unit costs changed with fallbacks and burst multi-tenant behavior.
[06:16] Marcus: Also embeddings cost were higher than expected when we started indexing more content, we need better caching there as well.
[06:23] Ravi: For embeddings we suggest local caching of vectors and incremental updates; Redwood also supports adaptive batching for embeddings which reduces per-vector cost. We'll include recommendations.
[06:33] Priya: I'll also pull the last 6 months of usage and create a forecast with seasonality adjustments for the proposal.
[06:40] Linda: On compliance, do you have any reference architecture for Private on-prem? We have a government customer that may require on-prem.
[06:48] Alex: Yes, we have an on-prem package and a private control plane pattern — I'll share the architecture doc. For on-prem the keys remain customer-managed and audit logs are shipped to your SIEM.
[06:59] Marcus: One more technical: how do you handle KV cache invalidation on model rollouts? We have concerns about stale context after a model version change.
[07:07] Ravi: We version cache keys with the model binary hash and rollout tags; when a model is rolled out we can choose to flush or keep caches and remap keys. For high-risk rollouts we recommend a canary and cache flush to avoid cross-version artifacts.
[07:22] Sofia: That should solve it.
[07:24] 
[07:40] Alex: Ok let's recap real quick — action items and owners. Alex will send pricing and reserved numbers by 7/2; Ravi will run the 1M token benchmark and share results by 7/7; Priya will share SOC2 and security docs by 7/1; Sofia will upload prompt set today. We schedule follow-up (commercial + tech review) week of 7/6.
[08:00] Linda: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:05] Marcus: Thanks.
[08:08] Priya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker overlap, some product names mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache), and minor punctuation issues.
